questions.q: What are the three buckets of the serviette strategy?
questions.why: Lesson 1 names the three tiers for everyday spending, long-term savings and wealth investments.

questions.q: What percentage of income goes into the Daily account?
a: 60 percent, for rent, food and other essentials
50 percent, for bills and the mortgage
questions.why: Lesson 1 allocates 60 percent to daily living and splits the rest between Splurge, Smile and debt.

questions.q: Why does Scott say to cut up your credit cards first?
a: It stops you adding more debt while you pay off what you owe
It improves your credit score immediately
It forces the bank to lower your interest
questions.why: Lesson 2 says destroying the cards removes the chance of piling on new debt during repayment.

questions.q: What should the Mojo account hold?
a: Three months of expenses for a bigger financial rough patch
One year of income for retirement
A deposit for a first home
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Mojo as long-term savings that should ideally cover three months of expenses.

questions.q: What does Scott recommend as a first investment?
a: Index funds that track a broad basket of stocks
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends index funds as a simple source of long-term, automated growth.
